loaderRecipe.preprocessHint: Stream split; filter lang in {C, C++}. Detection: X=func_before, y=vul. IMPORTANT: keep the `CWE ID` and `CVE ID` columns through preprocessing — they are needed for the per-CWE breakdown and the optional NVD CVSS join (do NOT drop them).

analysisRequirements.notes: Report detection F1 grouped by `CWE ID` as a results table AND a figure (bar chart, F1 per CWE, sorted descending). Collapse CWE types with <30 samples into an 'Other' bucket so per-group metrics are stable. Optionally stratify by NVD CVSS severity if data/nvd_cvss.csv is present (see nvd_enrich.py).

provenance.citation: Fan, Li, Wang, Nguyen — A C/C++ Code Vulnerability Dataset (Big-Vul), MSR 2020

loaderRecipe.preprocessHint: C functions from FFmpeg/QEMU. Detection: X=func, y=target.

analysisRequirements.notes: No `CWE ID` column in Devign — per-CWE breakdown does NOT apply here. This dataset's role is cross-dataset generalization (train on BigVul, test on Devign and vice-versa) to show the detector isn't overfit to one corpus.

provenance.citation: Zhou et al. — Devign, NeurIPS 2019 (via CodeXGLUE defect detection)

loaderRecipe.preprocessHint: Keep rows where vul==1 and lang in {C, C++}: func_before is vulnerable, func_after is the fix. These are the security patch pairs. Keep `CWE ID` and `CVE ID` columns for the per-CWE breakdown and NVD join.

analysisRequirements.notes: Report patch_correctness (and regression_rate) grouped by `CWE ID`. Collapse CWE types with <30 samples into 'Other'. Optionally stratify by NVD CVSS severity if data/nvd_cvss.csv is present.

provenance.citation: Fan et al. — Big-Vul, MSR 2020 (func_before->func_after security fix pairs)
